newsitem.title: USA: Avon falls on Brazil concerns - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Avon falls on Brazil concerns - analysts.

text.p: Avon Products Inc shares fell Thursday after the company reported second quarter earnings that matched Wall Street's expectations, but warned that its sales declined in Brazil, a key market for the company.
Analysts said Avon may also have suffered by comparison with Colgate-Palmolive Co, another personal products multinational that reported earnings above expectations.
"Overall, Avon had a good, not great quarter," J.P. Morgan analyst Michael Grant said. "I think there's probably some money going (from Avon) into Colgate. They had an excellent quarter."
Avon reported second quarter earnings of $0.72 per share, compared to $0.64 for the same period a year ago. First Call's consensus estimate was $0.72.
Colgate posted second quarter net income of $0.58 per share, up from $0.49 the year before. The First Call estimate was $0.56.
Avon was down 1-3/16 to 74-7/16 in afternoon New York Stock Exchange trading, while Colgate was up 5/8 to 76.
Avon said in a news release that its total international sales rose 10 percent for the quarter, and would have been up 16 percent except for the impact of the strong dollar.

But Avon said gains in Mexico, Venezuela and Argentina were offset by Brazil, where sales and pre-tax profits fell. Avon said the slump in Brazil was due to continuing softness in consumer spending and the company's ongoing inventory reduction programs.
"There were some cross-currents in the quarter," Morgan Stanley analyst Brenda Lowry said, citing Brazil as a concern.
From its opening at 75-5/8, Avon fell as low as 73-1/2 before recovering somewhat.
Grant said the dip probably reflected a temporary reaction to a high-multiple company not exceeding expectations, rather than a significant change in attitude toward Avon.
"I don't really see a change in expectations going forward," Grant said, adding that J.P. Morgan maintained its long-term buy rating on the company.
